title: Microsoft patents system to freeze games and inject ads during downtimes — watching commercials earns ad-free playtime credits
content: This patent uses the game engine and machine learning to determine the best time to serve an ad.

title: Massive 192GB GTA leak reveals early GTA VI map and canceled DLCs — files show liquid nitrogen death for Trevor and scrapped Liberty City expansion
content: The massive leak revealed early efforts in the development of GTA VI, as well as unreleased side missions, alternate endings, and even planned DLCs that never came to fruition.

title: Autonomous strike drone uses Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano to independently pick and bomb targets — Swedish startup's attack drones run small AI model, require no human input and zero external comms
content: Drones built with small, non-frontier computer-vision models autonomously identified and attacked targets in a recent demo.

title: Jensen Huang says there is '0% chance' AI destroys the world by 2030 — 'We should go as fast as we can, irrespective of anyone else,' dismisses Anthropic doom warnings and rejects new regulations
content: Chief executive of Nvidia claims that fears that AI will destroy humanity in the coming years are unsubstantiated as safety mechanisms can preserve that.

title: Charts: Two-thirds of Taiwan's chip equipment growth comes from testing AI chips
content: Taiwan's listed semiconductor equipment, components, and solutions suppliers are growing at nearly twice the pace of the chipmakers they serve, and most of that growth traces back to one step in the production flow: test.

title: BYD plans four Europe factories as EU tariff pressure rises
content: BYD is planning four factories in Europe over the long term as it works to meet local manufacturing rules and expand its customer base. The Chinese electric vehicle maker wants three vehicle assembly plants and one EV battery plant, according to company adviser and former Fiat Chrysler executive Alfredo Altavilla.

title: AI capacity crunch drives up consumer tech costs, deepening China's deflation
content: Surging AI server demand is reshaping consumer electronics. Memory costs have risen sharply this year, prompting Huawei, Oppo, Xiaomi and Apple to raise prices on some smartphones. A senior Chinese technology industry source said the increase reflects memory suppliers prioritising capacity and investment for AI products rather than stronger handset demand, which is squeezing smartphone memory supply.

title: Wiwynn brings cobots to L10 server assembly as AI rack testing drives factory redesign
content: Wiwynn is introducing collaborative robots (cobots) at its El Paso, Texas, facility and third plant in Mexico, alongside a central heat exchange system designed to support liquid-cooled server rack testing. The upgrades reflect the company's efforts to modernize manufacturing as AI servers become more complex and demand for liquid cooling increases.

title: Foxconn joins Quantron, Hongjing Drive in zero-emission commercial vehicle partnership
content: German commercial vehicle company Quantron and China's Hongjing Drive have formally agreed to establish a joint venture, Quantron China, to develop a China-Europe technology and industrial platform for next-generation zero-emission commercial vehicles. Foxconn will serve as the industrial manufacturing partner for truck and bus platforms, supporting their international deployment.

title: Chinese memory supply is disruptive to pricing, Acer's Jason Chen says, as shortages ease
content: PC component shortages are easing, Acer chairman and CEO Jason Chen said, with memory tight only at the high end of DDR5 and CPUs no longer in short supply. Suppliers across the bill of materials are still pushing through price increases, he said, some of them hard to justify. He expects PC prices to keep climbing before reversing in the second half of 2027.
